sŭb-armālis , e, adj. armus,
I.passing under the arms (post-class.): “vestis (perh. thrown back under the arm),” Mart. Cap. 5, § 426 .—As subst.: sŭbarmāle , is n., = subarmalis vestis, Valer. ap. Treb. Claud. 14; Spart. Sever. 6 fin.; Vop. Aur. 13; cf. subalaris.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
